topics.title: Business Mathematics
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Use a multiplier when calculating percentage change. (u, s)
Understand and calculate depreciation and appreciation. (u, s)
Understand and convert local and foreign currencies. (u, s)
Describe and determines Mortgage of assets. (u, s)
Calculate income tax given income tax bands. (u, v/a)

body.text: A multiplier turns a percentage change into a single number to multiply by. A 20% increase uses multiplier 1.20 (100%+20%); a 20% decrease uses multiplier 0.80 (100%-20%). Ashok invests UGX 100 000 at 10% compound interest per year: after 1 year it is worth 100 000 x 1.10 = 110 000; after 2 years, 110 000 x 1.10 = 121 000 — each year's interest is calculated on the new total, not the original amount.

body.expr: UGX 100 000 x 1.10 x 1.10 = UGX 121 000 after 2 years at 10% compound interest

body.text: Depreciation reduces an asset's value over time (e.g. a car losing value); appreciation increases it (e.g. land gaining value). Both use the same multiplier method, but depreciation's multiplier is below 1. A car worth UGX 20 000 000 depreciates by 15% per year: after 1 year it is worth 20 000 000 x 0.85 = UGX 17 000 000.

To convert currency, multiply by the exchange rate. If UGX 3 700 buys 1 US dollar, then UGX 500 000 converts to 500 000 ÷ 3 700 ≈ 135.14 US dollars. Hire purchase spreads the cost of an item over instalments, usually totalling more than the cash price because interest is included.
